names.lift_crank: Single-arm horn, from the bag, last hole
names.wrist_horn: Cross horn (from the bag), long arms cut to 11 mm
names.gripper_horn: Double-arm horn (from the bag), arms cut to 7 mm

1.fit: LM6UU into the carriage ×4: ~Ø12.25 as printed (13.3 in CAD, teardrop pockets: no support inside). Each bearing should slide in by hand. Loose: one wrap of electrical tape round the bearing. Tight: sandpaper on a dowel. Old carriage (pockets ~12.0 with support bits inside): clear the bits with a small screwdriver, then sand, or reprint.
1.how: Do this on the table, carriage on its own: 2 bearings from below, 2 from above, flush with the faces. No glue (a drop of superglue only if one is loose and tape doesn't hold). The bearings are optional for a first test: the carriage also slides on the bare rods, with more friction (see step 7).

2.fit: This joint must turn. The link's big hole is the pivot: it must swing freely on the screw (open it with a 5/32″ bit by hand if it binds).
2.how: Carriage on the table, nothing else on it yet. Lay the link's big hole over the carriage's small boss and drive ONE #6 × ¼″ pointed (sheet-metal) pan-head screw in sideways. Stop as soon as it is snug, then back off ¼ turn so the link swings. Use a ¼″ screw, not ½″: a longer one reaches the rod's path.

3.how: Spine on the table on its own. Push the lift servo's body through the spine's bracket from the left until its tabs sit on the bracket, then 2 servo-bag screws through the tabs. Its spline points left, out of the spine.

4.fit: The link must turn on the crank screw. Open the link's small hole to 3/32″ (2.4 mm) so the screw only bites the horn. The servo now swings 68° (LIFT_UP 98): the carriage rises 15.7 mm.
4.how: Do it in this order, everything still on the table: 1) Set the lift servo to 30° (laptop panel). 2) Take the single-arm horn from the servo bag (don't cut it) and screw the link's small hole onto its LAST hole (~14 mm from the centre): a servo-bag screw through the link into the horn. 3) Hold the carriage + link + horn up to the spine and press the horn onto the servo spline with the arm pointing toward the rods, tilted ~34° below horizontal (the nearest spline tooth; fine-tune LIFT_DOWN / LIFT_UP in the laptop panel). 4) The small centre screw through the horn into the spline. Now spine, servo, crank, link and carriage hang together.

6.how: Stand the spine (with the lift servo, crank, link and carriage hanging on it) on the turret plate behind the 2 rod holes. 2 × #6-32 from ABOVE through the spine's foot into the plate. Each screw head sits in a small half-round notch in the spine wall (old spine without the notch: file or Dremel a 1.5 mm half-round notch next to each hole, or use a #6 screw with a smaller head).

8.fit: Try-fit, both rods (~Ø5.95 as printed). Old cap: holes drilled 15/64″ by hand, 8 mm deep. Then the 2 screws. After: the carriage must still slide freely.
8.how: 2 × #6-32 from ABOVE through the cap into the top of the spine. The cap holds the rod tops in line (they can't come out of the plate) and ties the spine to the rods into one stiff frame. Drilling the cap's rod holes right through is fine: a rod a little too long then just sticks out.

10.fit: Gear mesh: try it on. Teeth engage with a little play and no binding over the full swing. Never sand or file gear teeth. Printers rarely print teeth exactly, so the file is made to be edited: if they bind, print the looser pair (cad/print/stl/finger_variants/, gear_thin 0.18 or 0.25); if they rattle, the tighter pair (0.00). Or set gear_thin in backend/cad/model.py and run backend/cad/finger_variants.py.
10.how: Before this step: lay the cut double-arm horn (step 12) on the left gear, hub up, centred, arms pointing front-to-back (toward the can and away from it), and drill 1/16″ pilots through its 2 holes into the gear; take the horn off again. Slide both fingers in together between the plates, both opened by the same angle, so the teeth mesh symmetrically.

11.fit: Ø3.9 mm running fit. The finger must swing freely on the axle. Tight: twist a 5/32 in drill through by hand.
11.how: #6-32 from the top through the frame and the right finger, threading into the bottom plate: it is the axle.

12.fit: Horn trimmed to Ø12 mm, flat on the gear. Cut the SG90 round horn down to Ø12 mm (flush cutters, then sand), keeping its 2 holes 5 mm from the centre (or drill 1.5 mm through the horn using the gear's pilots as the guide). A full-size horn hits the servo post. The spline must slide into the hub without force.
12.how: 1) The double-arm horn from the SG90 bag, both arms cut to 7 mm from the centre (14 mm long): it then turns inside the frame's 16 mm opening. 2) Turn the left finger so the horn's arms point front-to-back (toward the can) and drop it through the opening onto the gear, hub up (sideways it catches the servo post next to the opening), its 2 holes over the pilots you drilled before step 10, and drive the 2 small servo-bag screws (the shortest ones in the bag) through the horn into the gear. 3) SG90 at 20° (laptop panel). Hold the SG90 upside down over the frame so its spline points down into the horn's hub and the body lies over the 2 posts; press the spline fully in (turn the finger a little until the teeth engage). 4) 2 servo-bag screws through the SG90 tabs into the posts. Check: the fingers open and close together when you turn the servo by hand (unpowered).

13.how: Body through the arm's bracket from the front, 2 servo-bag screws through the tabs.

15.glue: Superglue the rubber pad to the frame where the can's side touches.
15.how: Cut 9 x 13.5 mm from the silicone sheet (or a rubber band / inner tube).

16.fit: 6807 into the base pocket: ~Ø47.0 as printed (48.0 in the CAD file; this printer makes holes ~1 mm small). Old base (46.0): open it with a sanding drum, low speed, all the way round, to 47.0. Too tight: sand the wall a little at a time. Loose: 1 layer of tape on the bearing.
16.how: Push on the OUTER ring only, evenly: flat block on top, squeeze in a vise or press with both thumbs. No glue.

17.how: 4 x #8-32 screws from UNDERNEATH: through the 4 holes in the servo's tabs, up into the 2 printed blocks inside the base. They cut their own thread in the plastic: snug, don't over-tighten (it strips).
17.fit: Spline height. A base printed before 25 Nov has its 2 servo blocks 5 mm too long (the old CAD had the MG996R 5 mm too tall), so the spline stops 5 mm short of the horn. Don't sand the blocks: they're inside the base and must stay level. Instead, put the horn on the spline where it is, drop the printed 5 mm horn spacer (cad/print/fix/horn_spacer_5mm.stl, 23 min) on it, and fix the turret plate with 4 × #2 × 5/8″ screws (the servo-bag screws are too short now). New base files are already corrected.

18.glue: Hot glue or tape the washers into the 2 back pockets: the pockets are open underneath, loose weight just stays on the table.
18.how: ~50 g of washers / coins / small rocks in each back pocket, glued in. Optional: 4 rubber feet or hot-glue dots under the base. A bag of sand or a handful of washers works as the weight.

20.glue: A dab of hot glue on each peg holds the Uno and the buck. The breadboard is self-adhesive.
20.how: Boards onto the printed pegs. Buck already set to 5.8 V (bench test).

21.how: Button, LED and DC jack go through the panel holes from the front; their nuts go on inside.

22.how: Tabs slide under the base wall, then 2 x #6-32 from UNDERNEATH through the tabs into the base.

5.how: On the table, before anything else is on the plate: put the MG996R round horn under the turret plate, inside the hub, its 4 inner holes lined up with the plate's 4 small holes. Drive 4 servo-bag screws DOWN through the plate into the horn (open the plate's 4 holes to 3/32″ / 2.4 mm first so the screws pull the plate onto the horn). The plate and horn are now one part: they go onto the servo at the very end (step 19).

7.fit: Rod ends into the turret plate: ~Ø5.95 as printed (7.05 in CAD): light press, straight down to the bottom. Too tight: open with a 15/64″ (5.95 mm) bit turned by hand. Then the slide test: Tilt the rods: the carriage must slide down by its own weight with no tight spot. Sticks: the tight pocket needs a little sanding. Without bearings it slides too, but needs ~1.5 N more from the lift servo and the printed bore wears in time.
7.how: Hold the carriage level over the rod holes. Push each rod down from the top: through the carriage's upper bearing, its lower bearing, then into its blind hole in the turret plate, all the way to the bottom. No screws, no glue: the top cap traps the rods next.

9.how: On the table. Take the wrist servo's cross horn from the bag and cut its two long arms to 11 mm from the centre (flush with the frame's 28 mm flange). Lay it on the flange with the hub facing AWAY from the frame (toward the servo), long arms horizontal, centre on the flange's centre. The flange has 4 pilots on the arms (2 on the long arms ~7.7 mm out, 2 on the short arms ~6 mm out): drive 4 servo-bag screws through the horn's holes into them. A hole that doesn't line up: drill 1/16″ through the horn hole into the flange.

14.how: Wrist servo at 0° first. Hold the whole claw (frame + horn + fingers + gripper servo) with the plates level and press the horn's hub onto the wrist servo's spline until it is fully on. No centre screw: the frame covers it, and the spline teeth carry the turning force.

19.fit: Hub into the 6807's inner ring: ~Ø34.9 as printed (34.3 in CAD). It should press in by hand and the plate must turn freely after. Too tight: sand the hub evenly while turning it. Loose: one wrap of tape on the hub.
19.how: Turntable servo at 135° first (laptop panel: Base 135). Lower the whole column straight down: the turret plate's hub goes into the bearing's inner ring and the horn (already screwed under the plate) onto the servo's spline; turn the column until the spline teeth engage, rod side facing the START can. No centre screw: the column covers it; its weight keeps the horn on the spline and the bearing carries the load. Check: the column turns smoothly by hand when the servo is unpowered.

precise.label: PRECISE FIT
precise.text: Press fits and alignment that decide whether the robot works (steps 1, 7, 16, 19). The holes are now corrected for this printer; test each fit with the real part, tape if loose, sand if tight.

try.label: TRY-FIT
try.text: Test before you tighten: it should turn, slide or mesh freely. Easy to fix with a drill bit by hand, a knife or sandpaper.

easy.label: EASY
easy.text: Screws into servo tabs, glue, boards on pegs. Any print quality works: do these while other parts are still printing.

while_waiting: Electronics bench test (PART E) and set the buck to 5.8 V
Set every servo to its angle (laptop panel) before it gets its horn
Cut the 2 rods to 112 mm, file the ends
Find the horns in the servo bags: single-arm (lift, step 4), cross (wrist, step 9), double-arm cut to 7 mm (gripper, step 12)
Cut the rubber pad 9 x 13.5 mm (step 15)
Build the whole column on the table (steps 1-15) while the base prints: it goes onto the base in step 19
tol_note: The fits are being re-measured: the first prints did not fit even with sanding. Use the tolerance re-check sheet (docs/17_tolerance_recheck.md) and send the measured sizes.
